methodology: MVP: Sleeper player search rank + actual league production (when available) + roster fit + starting-lineup impact.
headline: Parker Turns Tillman Into a Backfield Upgrade
verdict: Parker is the clear current winner, with an 84.1 overall score and a B grade against CJ’s 71.5 and C-.
summary: Parker acquires Javonte Williams, whose supplied market value of 64.9, search rank of 32, 17 games played, and 8.7 season average make this the stronger current asset exchange. The fit is not perfect: Parker already has six running backs, including Bijan Robinson and Alvin Kamara, while holding only four wide receivers. Still, moving Cedric Tillman—ranked 667th, with a 5.9 season average and a zero recent average—for Williams gives the 9-5 roster a more established backfield piece. CJ has seven wide receivers, so Tillman addresses positional quantity, but surrendering Williams creates the larger value loss. Even the King of Dogshit Trades can occasionally make the cleaner move.

sides.analysis: CJ’s cjbroadway23 receives Cedric Tillman for Javonte Williams, earning the deal’s weaker grade at 71.5 overall and C-. Tillman’s supplied value is 27.3, his search rank is 667th, and his 5.9 season average trails Williams’ 8.7; his recent average is also zero. The roster-fit argument is real: CJ has seven wide receivers, compared with five running backs, so adding another receiver matches the team’s positional construction.
